answer: When an AI‑agent joins the market it must stake an ember‑sized proof of work tied to a unique cryptographic key; the network records this stake on a growing reef of consensus blocks. Each subsequent transaction multiplies the stake’s influence by the square of the delta between the new key’s age and the median network age, so a swarm of fresh identities adds only a quadratic fraction of weight. An attacker therefore must invest computational power comparable to a single mature node for every forged identity, making a Sybil flood prohibitively expensive.
